headline: Cryptographers disagree over whether OpenAI's burst of AI-written maths papers means AI could one day break the encryption that protects online banking and messages.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the release is from 6 Oct and the article is expert opinion, not a new finding.
importance_line: Anyone who banks or messages online is affected only if a shortcut is found, which no one has shown, and experts mostly advise against panic while asking AI labs to say what they have tried.
summary: Scientific American reports that after OpenAI posted 722 AI-written maths manuscripts, Matthew Green, a cryptographer at Johns Hopkins University, put the chance of losing confidence in current public-key encryption at 15 percent, while Yehuda Lindell, a Bar-Ilan University professor and head of cryptography at Coinbase, sees "no evidence whatsoever" of a breakthrough. None of the 722 papers deals with cryptography, and the researchers quoted agree that no deployed algorithm has yet been broken by AI.
notes: Full text from fulltext file. Analysis of expert views; no new technical result.
